headline: Dry, cool weather continues through Tuesday with fog likely Monday morning; wetter, windier weather arrives Wednesday and especially Friday.
summary: A ridge of high pressure (an area of sinking air aloft) keeps western Washington dry through Monday. Sunday's thick low cloud and fog in the lowlands should give way to some sun breaks by mid to late afternoon, though skies stay mostly cloudy. Nights are cool, in the 30s, with some more frost in the early morning hours, and highs Sunday and Monday are seasonable, mainly in the low to mid 50s. Early Monday morning, light winds and leftover moisture near the ground will likely bring widespread fog and low cloud again, with areas of greatly reduced visibility. Forecasters were not confident enough to issue a Dense Fog Advisory but are watching it. From Monday night into Tuesday, a weakening system may bring some light precipitation to parts of the coast and Olympic Peninsula, while most of western Washington stays dry. Temperatures warm a few degrees on Tuesday, with lows from the mid 30s to mid 40s and highs from the mid 50s to low 60s. The second half of the week turns unsettled: a weak system crosses the area Wednesday, and a stronger one Friday will likely bring gusty winds, more widespread lowland rain and mountain snow. A brief break is possible Friday night into early Saturday, but more systems could arrive by Saturday evening. Forecasters are fairly confident in the dry start and wetter later pattern, including Friday's stronger system, but the pattern heading into next weekend, including how long the Friday-night break lasts, is still uncertain. No watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect on land. A Small Craft Advisory for rough seas covers the coastal waters and the west entrance of the Strait of Juan de Fuca from 1 AM Monday to 1 AM Tuesday.
